correctness.rationale: For the root-inclusive ancestor inverse B, the edge-difference energy has the extra term |g(root)|^2, so B*B is positive definite and is the ordinary Laplacian plus unit root grounding. On normalized levels and on each child contrast the edge coefficient is -sqrt(b); the sum-zero condition cancels parent coupling. At each level these spaces have the full dimension, giving the stated multiplicities, including the terminal 1x1 block. The determinant recurrence has final diagonal 1-lambda, giving exactly the stated Chebyshev subtraction. II* counts common ancestors and is strictly positive; its simple positive top mode is radial. Its leaf equation and backward difference recurrence give strictly increasing integrated values and hence a positive input. Independently, the lower-triangular radial integration matrix is the lower part of the rank-one array b^((i-j)/2): the omitted upper part has squared Frobenius norm at most (h+1)/(b-1), while the full rank-one norm is sqrt((sum b^i)(sum b^-j)). This gives the stated asymptotic. The path equation has g(-1)=0 and g(h+1)=g(h), giving the stated sine norm. Fresh replay at /workspace/review_replay.py (python3 /workspace/review_replay.py tree) used direct SVD of ancestor-incidence matrices, not the frozen inverse-check code: tested (b,h)=(1,5),(2,2),(2,4),(3,3),(5,2), with absolute full-spectrum discrepancies below 9e-14; also computed independent exact-sum enclosures of the scaled sharp norm. The numerical checks do not certify arbitrary depth. The depth asymptotic is for fixed b.

evidence: Multiply each output row at depth i by i+1. The previous trailing block starting at depth k becomes L_ij=b^((i-j)/2) for i>=j, on indices k,...,h, with multiplicity (b-1)b^(k-1); the full block has k=0. L^-1 is the unit lower bidiagonal with subdiagonal -sqrt(b); (L^-1)*L^-1 equals the frozen T. After reversing output depth, the earlier normalized radial Cesàro kernel converges in Hilbert–Schmidt norm to u⊗u with u_j=b^(-j/2), and norm b/(b-1). The deaveraged kernel is the earlier kernel times the row factor (h-r+1)/(h+1) at reversed row r. Extend that multiplier by zero beyond h; its norm is at most one and it converges strongly to identity. The Hilbert–Schmidt convergence is preserved by the triangle inequality and convergence on the rank-one limit.
